checks.title: Document is a quote / proposal, not a certificate
checks.check: Is the document a binding confirmation of cover in force, or an offer/quotation?
checks.reading: A quote proves nothing: the supplier may never have bound the policy. Quotes carry words like quote, proposal, premium, validity of offer, 'subject to'. A genuine certificate states that a policy IS in force with a policy number and period.

example.text: Title 'Commercial General Liability Quote'; premium shown; 'ICICI Lombard capacity (20%)'.

checks.explain: The document is a quotation, not a certificate of insurance in force.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate of insurance issued by the insurer confirming the policy in force (policy number, period, limits).

checks.title: Draft / specimen / 'for information only'
checks.check: Watermarks or notes indicating the document is not the final signed version.
checks.reading: Drafts and specimens are not evidence. Also catch 'projet', 'Entwurf', 'Muster', 'sample', 'void'.

example.text: Diagonal watermark 'DRAFT – NOT VALID' on every page.

checks.explain: The document is marked as a draft or specimen and cannot be relied upon.
checks.fix: Please provide the final, signed and stamped certificate.

checks.title: Policy schedule / excerpt of general conditions instead of a certificate
checks.check: The supplier sent pages of the policy wording (conditions, schedule) rather than a certificate addressed to a third party.
checks.reading: A policy excerpt can contain the right numbers but is not a certification by the insurer that the cover is in force today. Treat as structural; data may still be extracted for information.

example.text: 12-page PDF starting with 'Allgemeine Versicherungsbedingungen für die Haftpflichtversicherung (AHB)'.

checks.explain: The document is an excerpt of the policy, not a certificate confirming the cover in force.
checks.fix: Please ask your insurer to issue a certificate of insurance (attestation) summarising the cover in force.

checks.title: Cover letter / email only, certificate missing
checks.check: A broker or insurer letter says 'please find attached the certificate' but the attachment is absent.
checks.reading: Classify as EMAIL/COVER_LETTER. If the same file also contains the certificate (sample 09), keep only the certificate pages and record the letter as context.

example.text: Page 1 is a personal cover letter from the insurer's contact ('anbei erhalten Sie…'); the certificate follows on page 2.

checks.explain: Only a cover letter was received; the certificate itself is missing.
checks.fix: Please send the certificate referred to in your letter.

checks.title: Renewal notice, invoice or premium statement
checks.check: Financial documents mention the policy but do not certify the cover.
checks.reading: Premium invoices prove a payment, not the scope of cover, and often pre-date the period. Reject.

example.text: 'Avis d'échéance – prime annuelle TTC 12 340 €' with bank details.

checks.explain: The document is a premium invoice / renewal notice, not a certificate.
checks.fix: Please provide the certificate of insurance, not the premium invoice.

checks.title: Editable office file (DOCX/XLSX) instead of PDF/image
checks.reading: An editable file can be altered after issuance (Q31: DOCX = red flag). Block at ingestion without analysis.

example.text: attestation_RC_2025.docx uploaded in Ariba.

checks.explain: Editable file formats are not accepted for certificates.
checks.fix: Please upload the certificate as a PDF (or scanned image) exactly as issued by the insurer.

checks.title: Screenshot / photo of a screen, cropped or partial
checks.check: Image shows a browser window, phone UI, or only part of the page.
checks.reading: Partial captures hide sub-limits and signatures. Route to review if most fields extract; block if key zones are missing.

example.text: PNG 1080×1920 showing a phone screen with the top half of a certificate.

checks.explain: The file is a partial screenshot; parts of the certificate (signature zone, sub-limits) may be missing.
checks.fix: Please upload the full certificate as a PDF.

checks.title: Multi-document file (several certificates, several policies, attachments)
checks.check: One PDF contains more than one distinct document.
checks.reading: Split by document; analyse each; link them. Do not sum limits across different policies unless one document explicitly states it is an excess layer of the other (E20).

example.text: Cover letter + certificate in one PDF.

checks.explain: The file contains several documents; each has been analysed separately.

checks.title: Certificate references limits 'as per policy' without stating them
checks.check: Amounts are replaced by a reference to the policy or to general conditions.
checks.reading: Unverifiable. Critical guarantees → REQUEST_CHANGES (need figures).

example.text: 'Limits of indemnity: as per policy schedule.'

checks.explain: The certificate refers to the policy limits without stating amounts, which cannot be verified.
checks.fix: Please ask your insurer to state the limit of indemnity for each guarantee (amount, currency, basis).

checks.title: Blank template / unfilled fields
checks.check: Placeholder fields left empty or with brackets.
checks.reading: A template with empty insured name, dates or amounts is not a certificate.

example.text: 'Policyholder: ______________ Policy No.: XXXXXXX'.

checks.explain: The certificate contains unfilled template fields.
checks.fix: Please provide the completed certificate issued by your insurer.

checks.title: Document not about liability insurance (property, motor fleet, D&O, transport)
checks.check: The certificate covers another line of business.
checks.reading: Correctly identify the line. A motor or property certificate is structurally wrong for this request.

example.text: 'Certificate of Insurance – Property Damage and Business Interruption'.

checks.explain: The certificate relates to a different line of insurance (e.g. property / motor) and does not evidence liability cover.
checks.fix: Please provide the general & product liability certificate.

checks.title: Undated certificate
checks.check: No issue date and no period dates.
checks.reading: Without a date the certificate cannot be placed in time. DATES_PRESENT fails.

example.text: No 'Fait à… le', no period, only 'valid for the current insurance year'.

checks.explain: The certificate is undated and states no period of insurance.
checks.fix: Please provide a dated certificate stating the period of insurance (from / to).

checks.title: No insurer stamp / seal
checks.check: Presence of a stamp (ink or printed seal) attributable to the issuing insurer.
checks.reading: Richard: without a stamp the insurer can later deny having validated the document. Formal defect: the same certificate can be re-issued stamped. Detection = presence & attribution, not forgery detection.

example.text: Printed letterhead and signature, no stamp.

checks.explain: No insurer stamp was found on the certificate.
checks.fix: Please provide the certificate stamped by the insurer.

checks.title: No handwritten signature
checks.check: A handwritten-style signature of a person acting for the issuer.
checks.reading: Typed name only, or nothing. Formal defect.

example.text: Quote ends with 'Authorised Signatory' and no signature.

checks.explain: The certificate is not signed.
checks.fix: Please provide the certificate signed by an authorised representative of the insurer.

checks.title: 'Electronically generated – no signature required' disclaimer
checks.check: A printed note replacing the signature.
checks.reading: Common in DE/UK. Under the strict profile it fails SIGNATURE_PRESENT (formal). Profile switch `acceptElectronicSignatureNote` may allow it if a qualified e-signature (eIDAS) is embedded — check PDF signature field.

example.text: 'Dieses Schreiben wurde maschinell erstellt und ist auch ohne Unterschrift gültig.'

checks.explain: The certificate carries no handwritten signature; it states that it was generated electronically.
checks.fix: Please provide a signed certificate, or a PDF carrying a qualified electronic signature.

checks.title: Signature present but signer not named / no function
checks.check: A scribble without printed name or title.
checks.reading: Lower attribution confidence; route to review rather than block.

example.text: Stamp plus an illegible initial; no printed name.

checks.explain: A signature is present but the signatory is not identified.
checks.fix: Please ask your insurer to add the name and function of the signatory.

checks.title: Issued and signed by a broker (courtier / Makler / broker)
checks.check: Who signs: an insurer, or an intermediary?
checks.reading: A broker certifies what it believes; only the insurer binds itself. Richard: Marron & Associés → 'refus total'. Detect ORIAS numbers, 'courtier', 'assureur conseil', 'agent général', 'Makler', 'corredor', 'broker'. Profile option `allowAuthorisedBroker` (default false).

example.text: 'Agent Général MMA… immatriculé à l'ORIAS'; signed by the agency.

checks.explain: The certificate is issued by an intermediary (broker/agent), not by the insurer.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate issued and signed by the insurer itself (the broker may forward it).

checks.title: Broker letterhead but insurer stamp and signature present
checks.check: Mixed case: broker template, insurer authenticates.
checks.reading: Acceptable if the stamp and signature belong to the insurer and the insurer is named as issuer. Attribute the stamp; if stamp entity ≠ issuer → review.

example.text: Broker logo top-left, 'Pour l'assureur: AXA France IARD' with AXA stamp and signature bottom-right.

checks.explain: The certificate is on broker letterhead; the insurer's stamp and signature were verified.

checks.title: Insurer not found in the registry
checks.check: Issuer name resolved against the insurer registry (ACPR/EIOPA/BaFin/NAIC… curated JSON in POC).
checks.reading: Unknown carrier = cannot assess solidity. Block when no match and no regulator id on the document; review when fuzzy.

example.text: 'Global Trust Underwriters Ltd' – no match in EIOPA, no regulator number.

checks.explain: The issuing insurer could not be identified in the insurer registry.
checks.fix: Please confirm the full legal name and regulator registration of the insurer.

checks.title: Insurer rating below floor / in run-off / captive
checks.check: Financial strength rating vs profile floor (default A- AM Best / BBB+ S&P).
checks.reading: Weak or unrated carriers (Q19). Captive not fronted by a rated insurer → block (Q20). Mutual without rating → review.

example.text: Issuer 'XYZ Captive Re Ltd (Guernsey)' without fronting insurer.

checks.explain: The insurer's financial strength rating is below the required floor.
checks.fix: Please provide cover from an insurer rated at least A- (AM Best) or equivalent.

checks.title: Policy number missing
checks.check: Presence of a policy / contract number.
checks.reading: Every genuine certificate carries one (Richard). Needed in a claim. Formal defect.

example.text: Certificate with all limits but no contract reference anywhere.

checks.explain: No policy number is stated.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate stating the policy number.

checks.title: Policy number is a placeholder or inconsistent across pages
checks.reading: 'XXXXXX', '0000000', or header number ≠ stamp number → review (possible tampering or mixed documents).

example.text: Header: 'Policy 7854-221-A'; page 3 footer: 'Policy 7854-219-A'.

checks.explain: The policy number looks like a placeholder or differs between pages.
checks.fix: Please confirm the correct policy number.

checks.title: Co-insurance: capacity share < 100 % from the signing insurer
checks.reading: The signing insurer only carries its share. Forvia needs the whole tower evidenced: all co-insurers named and signed/stamped (Q14), shares summing to 100 %.

example.text: 'ICICI Lombard capacity (20%)'.

checks.explain: The certificate is issued by one co-insurer carrying only part of the limit; the other co-insurers are not evidenced.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate listing all co-insurers and their shares (100 %), signed by each, or issued by the leader on behalf of all.

checks.title: Co-insurers listed but only the leader signed
checks.check: Signature/stamp of each co-insurer, or a clause 'the leader signs on behalf of all'.
checks.reading: Block unless the leader's mandate is stated on the document.

example.text: 'Allianz 60 % – HDI 25 % – Helvetia 15 %' with one Allianz signature only.

checks.explain: Co-insurers are listed but have not signed or stamped the certificate.
checks.fix: Please have each co-insurer sign/stamp, or state the leader's authority to sign for all.

checks.title: Insurer contact is a generic webmail / no professional identifiers
checks.check: Email domain, phone, company registration numbers.
checks.reading: A certificate signed from gmail.com is suspicious. Review. Mask personal data in exports (GDPR).

example.text: 'For Allianz: j.muster@gmail.com'.

checks.explain: The issuer's contact details are not professional identifiers of the insurer.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate issued from the insurer's official channels.

checks.title: Standard disclaimer 'confers no rights on the certificate holder'

en: does not amend, extend or alter

checks.reading: Normal on certificates worldwide (ACORD, DE, FR). Do not penalise. Record as INFO.

example.text: 'This certificate is issued as a matter of information only…'

checks.explain: Standard disclaimer noted; no impact.

checks.title: Stamp belongs to a different entity than the issuer
checks.reading: Broker stamp on an insurer letter, or group stamp on a local entity. Review.

example.text: Letter from 'Zurich Insurance plc, Niederlassung Deutschland', stamp 'Müller Versicherungsmakler GmbH'.

checks.explain: The stamp does not match the issuing entity.
checks.fix: Please confirm which entity issued the certificate.

checks.title: Pasted / low-resolution stamp image
checks.check: Visual: stamp with uniform background rectangle, JPEG artefacts, identical pixel stamp on every page.
checks.reading: Not a forgery verdict (out of scope) — lower STAMP confidence → review.

example.text: Pixel-identical stamp at the same coordinates on pages 1–4, with a white rectangle behind it.

checks.explain: The stamp appears as a pasted image; authenticity could not be confirmed visually.
checks.fix: Please provide the original certificate (scan of the stamped original or the insurer's signed PDF).

checks.title: Insured name ≠ supplier legal entity in Ariba
checks.check: Normalised fuzzy match between Ariba supplier (legal name, country) and policyholder / named / additional / co-insured.
checks.reading: Q26: certificate must name the contracting entity; otherwise blocking (formal: the insurer can add the entity). Ignore legal-form noise (GmbH vs GmbH & Co. KG) only within the review band.

example.text: Ariba: 'Beyer Polyvlies Franz Beyer GmbH & Co. KG'; certificate: 'Beyer Holding GmbH'.

checks.explain: The certificate does not name the contracting supplier entity.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate naming {supplierLegalName} as policyholder or insured.

checks.title: Only the parent / group is named; supplier is a subsidiary
checks.reading: Acceptable only if the supplier is listed as co-insured/insured subsidiary (sample 10: Metraton under Landi Renzo master policy). Otherwise formal block.

example.text: Policyholder Landi Renzo S.p.A.; Metraton listed as insured company.

checks.explain: Only the parent company is insured; the supplier entity is not listed.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate confirming that {supplierLegalName} is an insured under the group policy.

checks.title: Supplier appears only as 'additional insured' added for a customer
checks.check: Role of the supplier on the certificate.
checks.reading: Additional insured status is acceptable (profile acceptAs). But if the supplier is added only for one project/contract, check scope wording.

example.text: 'Additional insured: XYZ S.r.l. in respect of contract no. 4711 only.'

checks.explain: The supplier is covered as additional insured.

checks.title: FORVIA entity named as additional insured
checks.check: A FORVIA company appears on the certificate.
checks.reading: Positive, not required. Record as OK; useful for buyers.

example.text: A FORVIA subsidiary listed as additional insured.

checks.explain: A FORVIA entity is named as additional insured on this policy.

checks.title: Shared limit across many co-insured companies
checks.check: Group certificate with N insured entities and one aggregate.
checks.reading: Limit is shared group-wide (sample 07: 16 entities). Not a breach, but reduces effective capacity. Display as INFO with the count.

example.text: 16 co-insured companies share €5M combined.

checks.explain: The annual aggregate is shared between {n} insured companies.

checks.title: Certificate addressed to another customer (another OEM)
checks.reading: Still evidence of cover if not restricted to that customer's contract. Review wording; INFO otherwise.

example.text: 'Certificate holder: Volkswagen AG, Konzerneinkauf'.

checks.explain: The certificate was issued for another customer; the cover described is not customer-specific.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate addressed to FORVIA or 'to whom it may concern'.

checks.title: Trading name / brand instead of legal name
checks.reading: Review band; ask for legal name if ambiguous.

example.text: Insured: 'AutoSeal' (brand); Ariba: 'Dichtungstechnik Müller GmbH'.

checks.explain: The insured is identified by a trading name; legal identity could not be confirmed.
checks.fix: Please confirm the legal name of the insured entity.

checks.title: Post-merger / renamed entity
checks.check: Insured name is the former name of the supplier.
checks.reading: Legal continuity usually preserves cover, but the certificate should be updated. Review.

example.text: Certificate: 'Faurecia Interior Systems'; Ariba: 'FORVIA Interior Systems'.

checks.explain: The certificate names a former legal name of the supplier.
checks.fix: Please provide an updated certificate with the current legal name.

checks.title: Insured address / country differs from supplier
checks.reading: Review: could be a sister company.

example.text: 'Copo Ibérica S.A.' (Spain) vs supplier 'Copo Brasil Ltda.'.

checks.explain: The insured entity is registered in a different country than the supplier.
checks.fix: Please confirm that the certificate covers {supplierLegalName}, {supplierCountry}.

checks.title: Entity named only in the cover letter, not on the certificate
checks.check: Letter says 'for our client X'; certificate names Y.
checks.reading: Only the certificate counts.

example.text: Letter: 'Bestätigung für Beyer Polyvlies GmbH & Co. KG'; certificate: 'Beyer Holding'.

checks.explain: The supplier is mentioned only in the cover letter; the certificate names a different entity.
checks.fix: Please provide a certificate naming {supplierLegalName}.

checks.title: Product liability missing (certificate covers recall only)
checks.reading: German recall-only certificates (Kfz-Rückruf) are common: they evidence recall, not product liability. The main GPTC guarantee (≥ €20M) is absent → REQUEST_CHANGES (ask for the general/product liability certificate too).

example.text: Titles 'Rückrufkostenversicherung' / 'Kfz-Rückruf' only.

checks.explain: Product liability cover is not evidenced; the certificate only covers recall.
checks.fix: Please provide the general & product liability certificate (≥ €20M per occurrence and in the aggregate).

checks.title: Product recall missing
checks.reading: Recall is the #1 automotive risk (Ferrari case: €5M paid by FORVIA). Missing → REQUEST_CHANGES.

example.text: GL/PL combined €5M, no recall line.

checks.explain: Product recall cover is not evidenced.
checks.fix: Please provide evidence of product recall cover (≥ €15M).

checks.title: 'Withdrawal costs' (frais de retrait) is not a full recall cover
checks.check: FR wording: 'frais de retrait' vs 'frais de rappel'.
checks.reading: Withdrawal = removing the product from the market/stock; recall = locating, removing from vehicles, replacing. Map 'frais de retrait' to PRODUCT_RECALL with flag `scope=WITHDRAWAL_ONLY`; compare amount to recall threshold; explain the nuance.

example.text: 'Frais de retrait : 305 000 €' under a €10M general limit.

checks.explain: Only withdrawal costs are covered; full recall costs (including removal from vehicles) are not evidenced.
checks.fix: Please confirm product recall cover including costs of locating, removing and replacing defective parts.

checks.title: Pure financial loss (DINC) missing
checks.reading: Loss with no prior material damage (line stop). GPTC ≥ €15M. Often absent or tiny in DE (Vermögensschäden 100k). Missing → REQUEST_CHANGES.

example.text: No financial-loss line.

checks.explain: Pure financial loss cover is not evidenced.
checks.fix: Please provide evidence of pure financial loss cover (≥ €15M).

checks.title: DIC vs DINC confusion (FR)
checks.reading: DIC follows a covered material damage; DINC is standalone. Many FR certificates show DIC only. Do NOT map DIC to PURE_FINANCIAL_LOSS. 'Dommages immatériels' without qualifier → UNCLEAR, review.

example.text: 'Dommages immatériels non consécutifs : 200 000 USD'; DIC not stated.

checks.explain: Only consequential immaterial damage (DIC) is covered; non-consequential (DINC) is not evidenced.
checks.fix: Please confirm cover for non-consequential immaterial damage (dommages immatériels non consécutifs).

checks.title: German 'Vermögensschäden': which kind?
checks.check: 'Vermögensschäden' may mean pure financial loss or be a small sub-cover in Betriebshaftpflicht.
checks.reading: Map to PURE_FINANCIAL_LOSS; amounts are usually 100k–1M, far below €15M → BELOW_MINIMUM. Check 'echte/reine' qualifier; 'unechte Vermögensschäden' = consequential (DIC).

example.text: 'Vermögensschäden: 250.000 EUR' in a Betriebshaftpflicht certificate.

checks.explain: Financial loss cover is limited to {amount}, below the €15M requirement.
checks.fix: Please increase pure financial loss cover to ≥ €15M or provide the extended product liability schedule showing the applicable limit.

checks.title: Extended product liability (erweiterte Produkthaftpflicht) bundle
checks.check: German schedule listing: Verbindungs-/Vermischungs-/Verarbeitungsschäden, Weiterverarbeitung, Aus- und Einbaukosten, Prüf- und Sortierkosten, Maschinenklausel.
checks.reading: This bundle IS the automotive supplier cover. Map the bundle to EXTENDED_PRODUCT_LIABILITY and each listed item to its own code (DISMANTLING_REFITTING, etc.). Bundle limit may be a sub-limit of the main PL limit.

example.text: Extended product liability €20M as part of the schedule.

checks.explain: Extended product liability is covered ({amount}).

checks.title: Dismantling & refitting / removal & reinstallation not stated
checks.reading: GPTC critical keyword. Cost of removing the defective part from vehicles. Secondary criterion (5 pts) — but if recall is present and dismantling absent, explain.
checks.explain: Dismantling and refitting costs are not evidenced.
checks.fix: Please confirm whether dismantling/refitting (removal and reinstallation) costs are covered.

checks.title: Assembly / disassembly wording
checks.reading: Treat as synonym group of DISMANTLING_REFITTING; report separately if labelled separately.
checks.explain: Assembly/disassembly costs are covered.

checks.title: 'Covered' / 'included' without an amount
checks.check: A guarantee marked as covered but no limit stated.
checks.reading: Cannot compare to threshold → COVERED_NO_AMOUNT. For critical guarantees → REQUEST_CHANGES (state the limit). Frequently the cover is 'included in the general limit' — if explicit, inherit (E07).

example.text: 'Product recall: Covered' without amount.

checks.explain: {guarantee} is marked as covered but no limit is stated.
checks.fix: Please state the limit of indemnity applicable to {guarantee}.

checks.title: 'Available on request' / optional cover not taken
checks.reading: 'On request', 'optional', 'can be added', 'not selected' = NOT covered.

example.text: 'Garantie rappel de produits : non souscrite'.

checks.explain: {guarantee} is listed as optional and has not been taken out.
checks.fix: Please subscribe the {guarantee} extension and provide an updated certificate.

checks.title: Combined single limit (GL + PL, sometimes + PFL)
checks.reading: Map to COMBINED_GL_PL; allocate to PRODUCT_LIABILITY per profile `cslAllocation` (default FULL; Q13 open). Display 'inherited from CSL' badge.

example.text: Single figure for general + product liability.

checks.explain: Product liability is inherited from a combined general & product liability limit of {amount}.

checks.title: Automotive recall (Kfz-Rückruf) vs generic recall
checks.check: German specialty cover for recall of vehicles by OEM/authority.

en: recall liability for automotive component suppliers

checks.reading: AUTOMOTIVE_RECALL counts toward PRODUCT_RECALL (max of both). Usually better suited than generic recall. Check whether it covers 'Eigenrückruf' (own) and 'Fremdrückruf' (third-party recall costs).

example.text: 'Kfz-Rückruf 5 Mio. EUR'.

checks.explain: Automotive recall liability of {amount} counts toward the recall requirement.

checks.title: Recall: own costs vs third-party costs
checks.check: Does the recall cover pay the insured's own recall (first party) and/or recall costs claimed by customers (third party)?

fr: frais de rappel engagés par les tiers

checks.reading: For FORVIA (the customer) the third-party/liability side matters. Many 'recall expenses' products are first-party only. Flag `recallScope`.

example.text: 'Product Recall Expense – first party only'.

checks.explain: The recall cover appears to be first-party only; recall costs claimed by customers may not be covered.
checks.fix: Please confirm that recall costs incurred by your customers (third-party recall liability) are covered.

checks.title: Inspection & sorting costs (Prüf- und Sortierkosten)

fr: frais de tri et de contrôle

checks.reading: Part of extended product liability; frequent claim in automotive. INFO/secondary.
checks.explain: Inspection and sorting costs are covered ({amount}).

checks.title: Professional indemnity / E&O confused with product liability
checks.check: 'RC professionnelle' in FR is often used loosely for general liability; E&O ≠ PL.
checks.reading: Map by content, not label. If the certificate only evidences PI/E&O → product liability missing.

example.text: Titled 'Attestation RC professionnelle' but content is general liability + products.

checks.explain: The certificate evidences professional indemnity, not product liability.
checks.fix: Please provide the product liability certificate.

checks.title: Employer's liability, motor, environmental lines listed — irrelevant to the request
checks.check: Extra lines on a multi-line certificate.
checks.reading: Keep as OTHER/INFO. Do not let them inflate scores. Pollution is secondary (not scored in POC).

example.text: Long list: tenants liability, valet parking, terrorism…

checks.explain: Additional lines of cover noted (no impact).

checks.title: Goods in custody / tooling (biens confiés)
checks.check: FORVIA-owned tooling at the supplier's site.
checks.reading: Nice to have. INFO.
checks.explain: Goods in care, custody and control are covered ({amount}).

checks.title: Product guarantee / efficacy (performance) cover
checks.reading: Rare; not required. INFO. Do not confuse with PFL.
checks.explain: Product efficacy cover noted.

checks.title: Serial loss clause
checks.check: Several claims from the same cause treated as one occurrence.
checks.reading: Matters for recall/PL: a serial defect counts as one claim (one limit, one deductible). INFO; show to expert.
checks.explain: Serial loss clause present: related claims are aggregated as one occurrence.

checks.title: USA / Canada extension explicitly included
checks.check: Territorial extension for North America with its own limit.
checks.reading: Positive (secondary criterion TERRITORY_USA_CANADA). If the USA/Canada limit is lower than the main limit, display both (E19).

example.text: USA/Canada included in the German schedule.

checks.explain: Cover extends to USA/Canada ({amount}).

checks.title: Headline limit high, recall/withdrawal sub-limit tiny
checks.check: Compare each sub-limit to its own threshold, never to the headline.
checks.reading: THE trap (Richard). €10M general, €305k withdrawal → recall compliance = BELOW_MINIMUM at €305k. Gap bar must show 305k vs 15M.

example.text: 'Tous dommages confondus 10 000 000 € … dont frais de retrait 305 000 €'.

checks.explain: Recall/withdrawal is sub-limited to {amount}, far below the €15M requirement, despite a {headline} general limit.
checks.fix: Please increase the recall sub-limit to ≥ €15M.

checks.title: Recall sub-limit inside a combined single limit
checks.reading: Sample 03: CHF 20M CSL, recall sub-limited to CHF 5M. Recall = 5M, not 20M.

example.text: CHF 20M CSL; 'Rückrufkosten CHF 5'000'000'.

checks.explain: Recall is sub-limited to {amount} within the {headline} combined limit.
checks.fix: Please increase the recall sub-limit to ≥ €15M.

checks.title: Per occurrence vs annual aggregate — which figure to compare
checks.reading: Profile `amountBasis` (default: prefer annual aggregate when both exist, Q12). If only per-occurrence is stated → use it and flag `basis=PER_OCCURRENCE_ONLY` (secondary AGGREGATE_BASIS not earned).
checks.explain: Limits are stated per occurrence only; no annual aggregate is evidenced.
checks.fix: Please state the annual aggregate limit.

checks.title: '5,000,000 / 10,000,000' = per claim / aggregate
checks.check: Two figures separated by a slash or 'and'.
checks.reading: First = per claim, second = annual aggregate (DE/FR convention). Do not read as a range.
checks.explain: Limit {perClaim} per claim / {aggregate} per year.

checks.title: German 'x-fach maximiert' (maximisation multiplier)
checks.check: '2-fach maximiert' = annual aggregate is twice the per-claim limit.
checks.reading: Compute aggregate = multiplier × per-claim. Record the multiplier.

example.text: 'Deckungssumme 10 Mio. EUR je Versicherungsfall, 2-fach maximiert'.

checks.explain: Annual aggregate = {multiplier} × per-claim limit.

checks.title: Limit 'inclusive of defence costs' / 'costs inclusive'
checks.check: Whether defence costs erode the limit.
checks.reading: Common in US/UK/IN forms. Weaker than 'in addition'. INFO; expert may care.
checks.explain: Defence costs are included within the limit.

checks.title: 'Included in the general limit' — inherit or not?
checks.check: Guarantee explicitly stated as included within the main limit, no own figure.

en: included in the limit of indemnity

checks.reading: If the wording explicitly says 'within the above limit', inherit the main limit with flag INHERITED. If it just says 'covered', do not inherit (D10).
checks.explain: {guarantee} is included within the {headline} limit (inherited).

checks.title: Very high deductible / self-insured retention
checks.reading: Q15 open: no points in POC. Report; flag if deductible ≥ 5 % of limit or ≥ €500k. SIR means the insured pays first.

example.text: 'claims paid in excess of the SIR'.

checks.explain: Deductible of {amount} per claim ({pct} of the limit).

checks.title: Deductible expressed as a percentage ('scoperto')
checks.reading: Record pct + minimum + maximum. INFO.
checks.explain: Deductible: {pct} of each loss, minimum {min}.

checks.title: Foreign currency — convert at ECB rate of the reference date
checks.check: USD, CHF, GBP, INR, PLN, CZK, HUF, RON, TRY, BRL, MXN, CNY, JPY, KRW…
checks.reading: Convert once, persist rate + date (Q28-29). Show original and EUR. Near-threshold results within ±3 % → REVIEW (FX drift).
checks.explain: {amountOriginal} converted to {amountEur} at ECB rate {rate} on {date}.

checks.title: Indian lakh / crore notation
checks.reading: 1 lakh = 100,000; 1 crore = 10,000,000. Indian digit grouping (2-2-3). Parse before converting.

example.text: 'INR 1,00,00,00,000' = INR 1 billion.

checks.explain: Amount stated in crore/lakh notation ({amountOriginal}).

checks.title: European vs Anglo-Saxon thousand/decimal separators
checks.reading: Parse per locale of the document, never by global regex. Sanity check: PL limits < 10,000 are almost certainly mis-parsed.

checks.title: Abbreviations: Mio., M€, k€, Mn, MM, bn, Md
checks.reading: Mio./M/Mn/MM = 10^6; k/T (DE 'TEUR') = 10^3; bn/Md/Mrd = 10^9. Currency may precede or follow.

example.text: '5 Mio. EUR'.

checks.title: Amount written in words differs from figures
checks.reading: Words prevail legally; flag mismatch → review.

example.text: 'EUR 5.000.000 (cinq cent mille euros)'.

checks.explain: The amount in words ({words}) differs from the figure ({figure}).
checks.fix: Please confirm the correct limit.

checks.title: Per-guarantee sub-limit table with 'per claim / per year' columns
checks.reading: Extract row × column faithfully; keep basis per cell.

example.text: Italian table 'per sinistro / per anno'.

checks.title: Capacity share applied to limits
checks.reading: Effective limit carried by the signing insurer = share × limit; but FORVIA needs 100 % evidenced (B11). Do not silently scale the limit: show both.

example.text: 20 % of INR 1bn.

checks.explain: Only {share} of the {limit} limit is carried by the signing insurer.
checks.fix: Please provide evidence for the full limit from all co-insurers.

checks.title: Limit shared across several guarantees and insureds (aggregate erosion)
checks.check: One aggregate for GL + PL + recall + 16 companies.
checks.reading: Compliant on paper, weaker in practice. INFO with explicit statement.
checks.explain: A single annual aggregate is shared across guarantees and insured companies.

checks.title: Sub-limit for USA/Canada lower than main limit
checks.check: Separate reduced limit for North America.
checks.reading: Record both; USA/Canada secondary criterion earned only if ≥ profile `usaCanadaMin` (default: presence).

example.text: 'Worldwide €20M; USA/Canada €5M'.

checks.explain: USA/Canada cover is limited to {amount} (main limit {headline}).

checks.title: Primary + excess / umbrella layers
checks.check: Two documents or two lines: primary €5M + excess €15M.
checks.reading: Sum only if the excess certificate names the same insured, the same underlying policy and period. Otherwise treat separately.

example.text: 'Excess Liability €15,000,000 xs €5,000,000 primary (Policy 123)'.

checks.explain: Primary {primary} plus excess layer {excess} = {total} (tower evidenced).
checks.fix: Please provide the excess/umbrella certificate referencing the primary policy.

checks.title: Amount threshold exactly at the limit after FX rounding
checks.reading: Binary rule says BELOW_MINIMUM; route to REVIEW when within ±3 % of threshold and the original currency ≠ EUR.
checks.explain: The converted amount ({amountEur}) is within 3 % of the threshold due to exchange rate.

checks.title: Unlimited / 'no limit' / 'illimité' statements
checks.check: Some jurisdictions (e.g. motor) state unlimited; rare in PL.
checks.reading: Treat as COMPLIANT with flag UNLIMITED; verify not a parsing error.
checks.explain: Limit stated as unlimited.

checks.title: Limit expressed per person / per property (BI/PD split)
checks.check: Separate limits for bodily injury and property damage.
checks.reading: Product liability for FORVIA is mainly PD + financial. Use the PD figure (or combined if stated); record the split.

example.text: Separate lines for corporels / matériels / immatériels.

checks.explain: Limits are split: bodily injury {bi}, property damage {pd}.

checks.title: Recall limit stated per 'campaign' or per 'recall event'
checks.reading: Map as per occurrence; note basis.
checks.explain: Recall limit is per recall campaign.

checks.title: Small 'typical' sub-limits that are NOT critical
checks.check: Pollution €500k–1M, goods in custody, keys, tenants' liability.
checks.reading: Do not let many small sub-limits trigger alarms. Only the three critical guarantees are thresholded.

example.text: 'Atteintes à l'environnement 500 000 €' (Richard: 'a bit low' but secondary).

checks.title: Limit conditional on a clause ('subject to', 'provided that')
checks.reading: Extract the condition verbatim; route to review.
checks.explain: The limit is conditional: "{condition}".
checks.fix: Please clarify the condition attached to the limit.

checks.title: USA / Canada excluded
checks.reading: Red flag for an automotive supplier (exports, OEM plants in US/MX). Critical exclusion → −10 points; expert may escalate. Not blocking under GPTC default (Q16 open).

example.text: 'Monde entier hors USA/Canada'.

checks.explain: Cover excludes claims in USA/Canada.
checks.fix: Please confirm whether USA/Canada cover can be added (extension and limit).

checks.title: Territory limited to Europe / home country
checks.reading: Same family as F01, more severe in practice. Penalty; show scope.
checks.explain: Territorial scope is limited to {territory}.
checks.fix: Please confirm worldwide cover (FORVIA plants and customers worldwide).

checks.title: Claims-made trigger

it: in base alla richiesta di risarcimento

checks.reading: Claims-made is weaker for a buyer (cover ends when the policy ends, unless run-off). −5 points; show retroactive date (F04).

example.text: 'Claims made basis'.

checks.explain: Policy is written on a claims-made basis.
checks.fix: Please confirm the retroactive date and any extended reporting period.

checks.title: Retroactive date / extended reporting period
checks.reading: Retroactive date after the start of supply = gap. Review when retroactive date > FORVIA relationship start.
checks.explain: Retroactive date {date}; extended reporting period {erp}.

checks.title: Exclusion of automotive safety-critical components
checks.check: Brakes, steering, airbags, seatbelts, tyres, fuel systems excluded.
checks.reading: Fatal for a Tier-2 automotive supplier: the parts FORVIA buys may be exactly those. Critical exclusion → −10; expert: block. Flag `criticalExclusion=AUTOMOTIVE_PARTS`.

example.text: 'Excluding: automobile critical parts – steering, brakes, tyres, seat belts, airbags…'

checks.explain: The policy excludes safety-critical automotive components ({list}).
checks.fix: Please confirm that the parts supplied to FORVIA are not within the excluded categories, or obtain removal of the exclusion.

checks.title: Exclusion of products for the automotive / aerospace industry
checks.reading: If automotive is excluded, the certificate is useless for FORVIA — treat as product liability MISSING. Aerospace exclusion is INFO.
checks.explain: Products supplied to the automotive industry are excluded.
checks.fix: Please provide cover that includes products supplied to the automotive industry.

checks.title: Pure financial loss explicitly excluded
checks.reading: Contradicts any PFL line → PFL = EXCLUDED (worse than missing).
checks.explain: Pure financial loss is expressly excluded.
checks.fix: Please obtain an endorsement covering pure financial loss (≥ €15M).

checks.title: Recall excluded
checks.reading: PRODUCT_RECALL = EXCLUDED.
checks.explain: Recall costs are expressly excluded.
checks.fix: Please obtain recall cover (≥ €15M).

checks.title: Contractual liability exclusion

de: vertragliche Haftung über die gesetzliche hinaus

checks.reading: Standard in most wordings (liability beyond law). Not critical per se, but FORVIA GPTC are contractual obligations. INFO; expert review if broad.
checks.explain: Standard contractual liability exclusion noted.

checks.title: Product efficacy / failure-to-perform exclusion
checks.check: Product does not do what it should, without damage.
checks.reading: Standard; the gap is covered by PFL in part. INFO.
checks.explain: Efficacy exclusion noted (standard).

checks.title: Known circumstances / prior claims exclusion
checks.reading: INFO.
checks.explain: Known circumstances exclusion noted (standard).

checks.title: Sanctions, war, terrorism, nuclear, asbestos exclusions
checks.reading: Never penalise. INFO only. Do not list them in the supplier email.
checks.explain: Market-standard exclusions noted.

checks.title: Cyber / data exclusion
checks.check: Cyber exclusion on liability policies (LMA5400 style).
checks.reading: INFO for parts; relevant if the supplier delivers software/ECUs — flag `softwareSupplier` in Ariba data if available.
checks.explain: Cyber exclusion noted.

checks.title: Punitive / exemplary damages excluded
checks.reading: Common, low impact. INFO.
checks.explain: Punitive damages exclusion noted.

checks.title: Exclusion of recall ordered by authority vs voluntary
checks.reading: If only authority-ordered recalls are covered, OEM-initiated recalls (the common case) are not. Review.
checks.explain: Recall cover applies only to recalls ordered by an authority.
checks.fix: Please confirm that customer-initiated (voluntary) recalls are covered.

checks.title: Exclusion of pure financial loss from 'loss of use'
checks.check: US forms: 'loss of use of tangible property not physically injured' sub-clause.
checks.reading: Partial PFL via 'loss of use' exception; never count it as €15M PFL. UNCLEAR → review.
checks.explain: Only limited 'loss of use' cover is evidenced; it does not equate to pure financial loss cover.
checks.fix: Please confirm explicit pure financial loss cover.

checks.title: Exclusion of damage to the insured's own product / work
checks.reading: Standard; recall/dismantling covers the gap partly. INFO.
checks.explain: Own-product damage exclusion noted (standard).

checks.title: Jurisdiction clause (courts) vs territory
checks.check: Where claims may be brought vs where damage occurs.
checks.reading: Distinguish 'territorial scope' (damage location) from 'jurisdiction' (court). A 'worldwide except US courts' clause is a USA exclusion in disguise.
checks.explain: Claims brought before USA/Canada courts are excluded (jurisdiction clause).
checks.fix: Please confirm whether USA/Canada jurisdiction can be included.

checks.title: Certificate expired at reference date
checks.reading: Structural block. Demo clock = 2025-04-15 (samples are 2024-25 certificates).
checks.explain: The certificate expired on {dateTo}.
checks.fix: Please provide the current certificate.

checks.title: Expires within the renewal window (e.g. < 60 days)
checks.reading: Not a defect, but schedule a reminder / request renewal now. INFO + task.

example.text: Swiss certificate with end-of-year expiry.

checks.explain: The certificate expires in {days} days.
checks.fix: Please send the renewed certificate as soon as available.

checks.title: Period starts in the future
checks.reading: Cover not yet in force today (renewal certificate sent early). Accept if gap ≤ 30 days and a current certificate exists; else review.
checks.explain: The cover starts on {dateFrom}, after the reference date.
checks.fix: Please also provide the certificate for the current period.

checks.title: Period shorter than 12 months / short-term policy
checks.reading: Unusual; may indicate a project policy. INFO.
checks.explain: Policy period is {months} months.

checks.title: Only 'valid until further notice' / tacit renewal, no end date
checks.reading: DE/FR: 'verlängert sich stillschweigend'. Need a validity date for the certificate itself. If the certificate states its own validity (e.g. 'valid until 31/12/2025') use it; otherwise DATES_PRESENT → review.

example.text: German tacit-renewal wording alongside the period.

checks.explain: No end date is stated; the certificate refers to tacit renewal.
checks.fix: Please state the current insurance period (from / to).

checks.title: Issue date much older than the period / stale certificate
checks.reading: Even if the period is still open, an old certificate may not reflect mid-term changes. INFO; expert option to require ≤ 12-month-old certificates.
checks.explain: Certificate issued {months} months ago.

checks.title: Issue date after the start of the period (normal) vs before (check)
checks.reading: Issuing after inception is normal. Issued before the policy even existed → review.
checks.explain: The issue date precedes the policy inception by {days} days.

checks.title: Date format ambiguity (DD/MM vs MM/DD)
checks.reading: Resolve by document locale/language; if both readings are plausible and change the expiry verdict → review.

example.text: Indian document with US-style dates.

checks.explain: The date format is ambiguous.

checks.title: Cancellation clause ('may be cancelled at any time')
checks.reading: Normal. INFO. Some certificates promise notice to the certificate holder — positive.
checks.explain: Cancellation notice clause noted.

checks.title: Bilingual certificate: figures differ between languages
checks.reading: Extract both; if they differ → review; the original-language version usually prevails (check 'prevailing language' clause).

example.text: Bilingual layouts.

checks.explain: The two language versions state different figures.
checks.fix: Please confirm the correct limits.

checks.title: Summary table vs narrative text disagree
checks.reading: Review; prefer the more specific statement; show both.
checks.explain: The summary table and the text state different amounts for {guarantee}.
checks.fix: Please confirm the applicable limit.

checks.title: Text layer garbled / absent → OCR fallback
checks.check: Text extraction yields noise or nothing.
checks.reading: Run OCR (tesseract) and vision extraction; lower IAS; route to review if critical fields < 0.6.

example.text: Corrupted text layer.

checks.explain: The PDF text layer was unusable; values were read by OCR and may need confirmation.

checks.title: Low-resolution or skewed scan
checks.reading: Deskew, upscale; lower confidence. If signature/stamp zones unreadable → formal gates to review.

example.text: Scanned certificate.

checks.explain: Scan quality is low; some values have reduced confidence.
checks.fix: Please upload a higher-quality scan.

checks.title: Handwritten amendments on a printed certificate
checks.reading: Suspicious unless initialled and stamped. Review.
checks.explain: The certificate contains handwritten amendments.
checks.fix: Please provide a clean re-issued certificate.

checks.title: Page missing ('page 2 of 3' but 2 pages)
checks.reading: Incomplete document → review (sub-limits often on the last page).
checks.explain: The document appears incomplete ({have} of {total} pages).
checks.fix: Please upload the complete certificate.

checks.title: Insured name spelled differently across pages
checks.reading: Minor typos → ignore; different entities → review.
checks.explain: The insured name varies across pages.
checks.fix: Please confirm the legal name of the insured.

checks.title: Personal data present (names, emails, phone numbers)
checks.reading: Mask in exports, logs and emails; keep in the stored document. Not a defect.

example.text: Insurer employee's direct email on the cover letter.

checks.explain: Personal data detected and masked in exports.

checks.title: Multiple currencies on one certificate
checks.check: E.g. limits in EUR, deductible in CHF.
checks.reading: Convert each with its own currency; never assume one currency per document.
checks.explain: The certificate uses several currencies.

checks.title: Language not in the supported set / mixed scripts
checks.reading: Extraction still attempted (LLM multilingual); IAS lowered; route to review if < 0.75.
checks.explain: Document language ({lang}) has limited validation coverage; values should be confirmed.

checks.title: Certificate for the right supplier but the wrong FORVIA request (duplicate / re-upload)
checks.reading: Deduplicate by hash; link to the previous analysis; do not re-bill the LLM.
checks.explain: This document was already analysed on {date}.
